items.definition: A regular underlying beat.
The speed of the pulse, with a stated beat unit.
Beats per minute; specify quarter, dotted quarter or another unit.
A group of beats defined by the meter.
The repeating organisation of beats and subdivisions.
A smaller equal division of a beat.
A duration equal to one quarter of a whole note.
Half the duration of a quarter note.
One quarter the duration of a quarter note.
A note length increased by half its original value.
Three equal events fitted into the time normally occupied by two of the same written value.
A measured period of silence.
A link joining durations of the same pitch into one sustained sound.

Unequal subdivision placement whose feel varies with tempo and style.
A deliberately emphasised attack.
Relative loudness and its changes.
How a note begins, connects and ends.
Shortened, separated note articulation.
A connected articulation between notes.
How high or low a tone sounds.
The smallest step in standard twelve-tone equal temperament; one fret on this bass.
Two semitones.
Twelve semitones; a doubling or halving of frequency.
The distance between two pitches, described by letter span and quality.
The note used to name and organise a chord.
The tonal centre or first degree of a key.
A numbered relationship to a scale tonic.
An ordered pitch collection within a musical context.
A tonal framework centred on a tonic.
A three-note chord often built from root, third and fifth.
Chord tones sounded in sequence.
A pitch belonging to the currently considered chord.
A note connecting more structural notes.
A note chosen to lead into a target.
A major triad plus a minor seventh.

A chord symbol with a specified bass pitch after the slash.
A chord arrangement with a chord member other than the root in the bass.

A string-and-fret representation; rhythm must also be specified.
The F clef used to locate pitches on a staff.
A direct-injection device or connection method for routing an instrument signal.
